t.7.98.1: Urged on by Rāma's command, those swift-footed messengers set out quickly for Madhurā, and they made no halt along the way.
t.7.98.2: Then, having reached Madhurā in three days and nights, they related to Śatrughna all of that exactly as it had happened.
t.7.98.3: The abandonment of Lakṣmaṇa and the vow of Rāghava, the consecration of the two sons, and likewise the following of the citizens.
t.7.98.4: On the slopes of the Vindhya mountain was the delightful city of Kuśa; it was made by the wise Rāma and called by the name Kuśāvatī.
t.7.98.6: Having thus quickly reported everything to the great-souled Śatrughna, the messengers then fell silent, saying, "Hurry, O king!"
t.7.98.5: And the delightful city named Śrāvatī was proclaimed as Lava's; they also told of Ayodhyā left empty of people, and of Bharata following Rāghava.
t.7.98.7: Having heard of that dreadful-seeming destruction of the lineage that had come upon them, he gathered together the subjects, along with gold and the family priest.
t.7.98.9: Then that heroic lord of men consecrated his two sons; Subāhu obtained Madhurā, and Śatrughātī obtained Vaidiśa.
t.7.98.8: Raghunandana, having related to them everything just as it had happened, and also the impending reversal of his own state together with his brothers,
t.7.98.10: Dividing that army of Madhurā in two between his two sons, he established them both as kings, endowed with wealth and grain.
t.7.98.12: He beheld the great-souled one, blazing like a fire, clad in fine garments of linen, together with the imperishable sages.
t.7.98.11: Then, having taken leave of King Śatrughātin at Vaidiśa, Rāghava hastened to Ayodhyā with a single chariot.
t.7.98.13: Then, having saluted Rāma with joined palms and with his senses restrained, he who knew dharma spoke these words, reflecting on dharma alone.
t.7.98.14: Having performed with riches the fitting consecration of your two sons, the Rāghavas, know, O king, that I have firmly resolved to follow you.
t.7.98.16: Perceiving that resolute, unfaltering resolve of his, Rāma, the delight of the Raghus, spoke these words to Śatrughna: "So be it."
t.7.98.15: Nothing more need be said here, for your command is hard to transgress. Yet you ought not to abandon me, O hero, especially since I am devoted to you.
t.7.98.17: At the close of that speech, monkeys able to take any form at will, and hosts of bears and rākṣasas, came flocking together in great numbers.
t.7.98.18: The sons of the gods, the sons of the ṛṣis, and likewise the sons of the gandharvas, having learned of Rāma's departure from the world, all assembled there.
t.7.98.19: All of them, having assembled, saluted Rāma and said: "O king, O greatly glorious one, we have come to follow you."
t.7.98.20: O Rāma, bull among men, if you should go without us, it would be as though you had raised the staff of Yama and struck us down.
t.7.98.21: Having thus heard the words of the bears, monkeys and rākṣasas, he then spoke sweetly to Vibhīṣaṇa in a gentle voice.
t.7.98.23: Protect the people in accordance with dharma; you ought not to speak a word in reply.
t.7.98.22: As long as the people endure, so long, O Vibhīṣaṇa, mighty lord of the rākṣasas, shall you, dwelling in Laṅkā, hold what is your own.
t.7.98.24: Having spoken thus to him, Kākutstha then said to Hanūmān: "You have set your mind on living; do not break your promise."
t.7.98.25: O lord of the monkeys, as long as tales of me shall circulate in the world, so long shall you hold on to your life and keep your promise.
t.7.98.26: Having spoken thus, Kākutstha, Rāghava, then said to all those bears and monkeys, "Each one will set out together with me."
